newsitem.title: USA: ITT back on defense with new Hilton bid-arbs. [CORRECTED 21:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: ITT back on defense with new Hilton bid-arbs. [CORRECTED 21:40 GMT]

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp put ITT Corp back on the defensive in their six-month takeover war with a surprisingly large bid increase Wednesday, to $70 per ITT share from $55, a price arbitrageurs said could lead to a takeover.

"This is really aggressive of Hilton. It gives ITT shareholders a choice and is going to focus everything on the ITT shareholder meeting in November. ITT is running out of rabbits to pull out of the hat. People always assumed $70 (per share) would be the top, what was needed for Hilton to win this," said an arb who requested anonymity.
"They went right to the magic number. They are not going to nickel and dime. They truly want the company," he added.

A second arb, who asked not to be indentified, said, "I think they (Hilton) are going to have a hard time convincing Hilton shareholders that this is worth it. It has become a war of egos and the price is getting into the stratosphere, but I think it might be enough to get the deal done."

"The market assessed the value of the ITT split-up plan, and it is materially below the (new) Hilton offer. I suspect this will win the day, but it is going to require acquiescence of the ITT (corrects from Hilton) board. This could do it," the second arb added.
In early-session trade Wednesday, ITT shares climbed 2-13/16 to 65-4/4 while Hilton shed 5/16 to 32-7/16.

Last month, ITT said it would break into three separate companies, repurchase stock at $70 per share, and refinance debt, moves all designed to defend against Hilton's attempted raid, now worth $11.5 billion including debt assumption.
Yesterday in a federal court in Nevada, Hilton filed suit to block ITT's planned break-up.
A third arb, who asked not to be named, said, "Hilton is giving (ITT shareholders) a choice" between its $70 per share cash-and-stock offer and ITT's $70 per share tender.

"Hilton is there and they are clearly interested and going to continue to pursue this. They are not going to be scared off by ITT coming up with a game plan of its own. Hilton is a player," he said. "There was some sense that Hilton was going to let the ITT offer collapse under its own weight."

"There are a lot of moving parts (in the ITT plan) and sometimes that is not a positive in a transaction. Sometimes too many moving parts can be viewed as a negative, and that can rub shareholders the wrong way. The old slice and dice financial plan and some point begins to look like puree," he added.
